studies.question: What do the preview images look like; do dates line up; does brightness drift?
studies.method: Per-date brightness, stable-pixel drift, alignment and quality checks on the preview stacks of the first three places.
studies.result: Dates in Armenia were off by up to 6.9 pixels (fixed in the loader to under 0.1 pixel); the 6 October HV channel is off; at Tonle Sap the open-water-like area went from about 4,770 km2 (19 June) to about 7,980 km2 (17 October) at the EDA threshold. The 'biggest jump 11-23 September' in this note was later contradicted (V02).
studies.verdict: shipped (conditioning in the shared loader); early area numbers superseded

studies.question: Can plain mathematics (no learning) map open water, water under vegetation and the date of change?
studies.method: Two-threshold hysteresis water rule, two-state flooded-vegetation rule, CUSUM change point, all in PyTorch.
studies.result: Tonle Sap open water 2,234 to 3,837 km2 (first to last date); balanced accuracy 99.57 % on held-out Landsat anchors (scoreboard row 'math + terrain').
studies.verdict: shipped (the baseline and a fusion expert); the strict detector is a lower bound for the floodplain

studies.question: Can the flooded-vegetation layer be made stable?
studies.method: Rebuilt rule: self-calibrated HH-HV rise, a going-under state and water-distance context; threshold sweeps; Armenia as a negative control.
studies.result: Peak area moves at most 1.53x when a threshold changes (old rule 7.8x); Armenia false alarms fell from 39 km2 to at most 1.4 km2; 77 % of the area lies inside the Landsat maximum extent (old rule 40 %). Area at the 30 August peak about 1,600-2,500 km2; not validated (no reference map).
studies.verdict: shipped (water-under-vegetation layer)

studies.question: Can false 'water' on mountains be removed without any water reference?
studies.method: Mask from the Copernicus elevation model only: flat, low, and not in radar shadow. Landsat used only afterwards to measure.
studies.result: Sevan false water removed 70 % (150.7 to 45.3 km2) with 0.5 km2 of true lake lost (0.04 %); Ararat Valley 90 % removed; Tonle Sap nothing removed.
studies.verdict: shipped (hard mask in every area with a DEM)

studies.question: Can a change map have a stated false-alarm rate?
studies.method: Omnibus gamma-speckle test with an empirical null from stable land and false-discovery-rate control at 1 %.
studies.result: False alarms on held-out stable land at Tonle Sap 0.02 % (change-point method 5.8 %); 0 % at Sevan and Ararat.
studies.verdict: shipped (own 'sig' layer and the area ranges); rejected as a water expert

studies.question: Do Gaussian mixtures plus a hidden Markov model (probabilistic detector) beat thresholds?
studies.method: EM-fitted mixtures per area as emissions of an HMM over the ten dates, Baum-Welch transitions, a phantom slot for the outage.
studies.result: Sevan 1,235.3 km2 largest body on every date (published 1,242); Ararat 0 km2 false water; but Tonle Sap 17 October only 3,326 km2 against 3,837 km2 for the math detector.
studies.verdict: evaluated only (per-date mixture rejected by the admission rule, Sevan accuracy -0.66 pp; the HMM mask is the lake fallback)

studies.question: Do graph and spectral methods help?
studies.method: Random walker, total-variation cut, structure-consistency change, Laplacian eigenvectors and spectral clusters on the pixel grid.
studies.result: 0 km2 of false water in Armenia with no elevation data and Sevan calm dates within 0.1 % of 1,242 km2; but Tonle Sap flood grows only 1.2x (2,308 to 2,767 km2) and the normalised cut overlaps Sevan water with IoU 0.28.
studies.verdict: rejected as an expert (Tonle Sap accuracy -0.28 pp); spectral clustering dropped (follows geography)

studies.question: Can shoreline pixels get a water fraction instead of yes/no?
studies.method: Power-domain linear mixing between pure water and nearby land; checked against 30 m Landsat water at Lake Sevan.
studies.result: Calm-date lake area error against the published 1,242 km2 from -16 km2 to +0.5 km2 (1,242.5 km2); median shoreline distance to the 30 m shoreline 52-63 m instead of 84-107 m; a single pixel's fraction is still poor (RMSE about 0.35).
studies.verdict: shipped as a fusion v2 expert (Sevan only)

studies.question: Do better thresholds exist, found against an independent reference?
studies.method: Tune on one strip of the map against Landsat water, validate on a second strip, adoption gate fixed before the TEST strip was read.
studies.result: Tuned candidate J_test 1.0875 against 1.0900 for the old thresholds; worse at Sevan and Ararat.
studies.verdict: rejected (old thresholds kept; the procedure is the result)

studies.question: Can many detectors be compared on one table and fused, with a rule written in advance?
studies.method: Scoreboard (same pixels, labels, split, bootstrap intervals) and fusion v1: log-linear pooling, two-state Markov chain, 3x3 smoothing, admission rule.
studies.result: v1 admitted terrain, time, space, U-Net, deep autoencoder, sub-pixel; rejected GMM per date, graph, math score, stats confidence, flood-order mask, supervised network. Sevan dip 65.7 to 0.8 km2. But v1 lost about 700 km2 of the Tonle Sap flood (3,120 against 3,837 km2) because the rule never measured the floodplain.
studies.verdict: replaced by fusion v2 (v1 kept as documented experiment)

studies.question: Can one detector cover lakes, mountains and floodplains?
studies.method: Fusion v2: transition probability depends on observed darkening (0.3 % vs 65 %), reference-free floodplain zone with relaxed threshold, seeded detector as expert; rule 'RULE2' fixed before the TEST strip was read again.
studies.result: Tonle Sap 17 October 5,046 km2 (range 4,196-6,051; results.json) against an independent 5,421 km2 (4,198-7,222); inside the range on 7 of 10 passes (v1 and math: 1 of 10); mean area error 8.5 % (v1 25 %, math 20 %). Balanced accuracy 99.97 % Tonle Sap, 99.92 % Sevan. Only 76 % of the water lies inside the independent map; the floodplain threshold was fitted to the same estimate (in-sample).
studies.verdict: shipped (water source for every water place)

studies.question: Can the detector work on previews whose brightness stretch differs in every scene?
studies.method: Seeded detector: finds the scene's own dark population, measures each date relative to it; no absolute brightness. Leave-one-scene-out settings.
studies.result: Pantanal balanced accuracy 0.500 to 1.000 (0.994 leave-one-out), Lake Chad 0.503 to 0.991 (0.976); Nile delta not rescued (AUC 0.86, best single threshold 0.87).
studies.verdict: shipped as a fusion v2 expert (weight 0.37) and the per-scene switch

studies.question: Can bad passes be found automatically?
studies.method: More than twenty checks per pass and channel on stable land (gain, contrast, balance, slope, leave-one-out, misregistration, metadata); a failed channel is replaced by the median of the others.
studies.result: 134 passes in 15 areas: 3 pass-channels fail, 19 warn, 112 ok. Armenia 6 October HV fails (4.6x usual departure, z = -12). No false alarm on Tonle Sap flood dates. Removing the bad HV pass halves HV temporal sd at Ararat (0.0250 to 0.0117).
studies.verdict: shipped (runs before detection; flags shown in the app)

studies.question: Can the flood be dated pass by pass, also through the 24-day outage?
studies.method: Interpolated first-flood date between consecutive shorelines; leave-one-pass-out test; relative height from flood order checked against an elevation model; per-pixel logistic step ('choreography').
studies.result: 309 km2 flooded across the outage at 12.9 km2/day (9.3 before, 13.6 after): no hidden surge; hidden-pass area error 82 km2 against 161 km2 ('nothing changed'). Flood-order height against the elevation model rank correlation 0.45 (0.25 without its flattened water), against Landsat frequency -0.47; step date agrees with change point (0.95).
studies.verdict: shipped (arrival and choreography layers for Tonle Sap)

studies.question: Do our water maps agree with 38 years of Landsat water maps?
studies.method: Pixel agreement with JRC Global Surface Water (occurrence, extent, seasonality) on our windows.
studies.result: Permanent-water IoU 0.94 at Sevan and 0.84 at Tonle Sap (occurrence at least 75 %).
studies.verdict: evidence for the shipped detector (JRC ends in 2021)

studies.question: Are our 2026 claims right (wind at Sevan, rain in Armenia, flood timing at Tonle Sap)?
studies.method: Weather reanalysis and stations, river gauges and satellite altimetry against our area series; no radar images loaded.
studies.result: Tonle Sap open-water area follows NASA/USDA altimetry: Pearson 0.959, Spearman 0.976 (n = 10). Corrected: 'flood arrived late' contradicted (rise began early July, seen as water under vegetation; peak 24-29 September); Armenia 6 October HV not caused by rain (0-1 mm); Sevan wind claim undecided (31 August was a rain night, 29 mm).
studies.verdict: evidence; two claims corrected, wording changed in the stories

studies.question: How big was the 2026 Tonle Sap flood, without any radar?
studies.method: Expected flooded area from the measured lake level and the 38-year Landsat occurrence record (level to exceedance to occurrence), calibrated floodplain threshold.
studies.result: 17 October 5,421 km2 (plausible range 4,198-7,222) against 3,837 km2 for the strict detector (x1.41). A fitted threshold of 0.202 matches but gives 1,467 km2 at Sevan (should be 1,242 +/- 107): one threshold cannot serve both places. The estimate is a model; it shares its Landsat source with our labels.
studies.verdict: reference only; led to fusion v2

studies.question: Do our water maps agree with NASA's OPERA DSWx products?
studies.method: Compare with OPERA DSWx-S1 (C-band radar) and DSWx-HLS (optical) at 15 places; agreement between two products, not accuracy.
studies.result: Sevan IoU 0.97; Tonle Sap IoU 0.70 (preview) and 0.72 (calibrated), but 0.56-0.65 from mid-August when the flood enters the forest. Over 101 place-dates at 15 places: 93.8 % of pixels agree, balanced accuracy 0.72, mean IoU 0.38 (0.32-0.44). Weak at Inner Niger, Lake Chad, Urmia and others (see negative results). Tonle Sap 17 October: ours 5,046, OPERA S1 4,373 km2.
studies.verdict: evaluated; limits added to the record (no claim of being better)

studies.question: Can calibrated NISAR GCOV be used without downloading multi-GB files?
studies.method: A small remote server opens each remote HDF5 file by range requests, reads only the area window and returns a reduced file; the laptop writes GeoTIFFs.
studies.result: Ten Tonle Sap dates (80 m) and eight each of Sevan and Ararat (30 m) extracted; about 40 MB per date back for Tonle Sap. Data are PROVISIONAL (P05023).
studies.verdict: shipped as a data path (extraction code); Armenia calibrated data not in the app

studies.question: Does calibration narrow the Tonle Sap flood-size uncertainty?
studies.method: dB water rule tuned on one strip, tested on another, on all ten dates at 80 m; same independent estimate and altimeter.
studies.result: Balanced accuracy 0.995; 17 October 5,625 km2; mean deviation from the independent estimate 5.9 % (preview math 20.1 %, fusion v2 8.5 %); inside the range on 7 of 10 dates; area moves by 1.25x over the justified threshold range at the peak (previews 2.39x). The same thresholds give 0 km2 at Sevan (noise floor 7-8 dB higher). Calibration PROVISIONAL.
studies.verdict: shipped as its own app place (tonle-sap-cal); summary docs still say 'not in the app' (see limits)

studies.question: Does radar phase show what amplitude previews could not (Ararat Valley farming; ground motion; soil moisture; Tonle Sap onset)?
studies.method: NISAR GUNW coherence, phase and SME2 soil moisture at Ararat, Sevan and Tonle Sap; foothills, Yerevan and Sevan as controls.
studies.result: Coherence below 0.3 on 43-44 % of the valley floor in June-July, 22-25 % from mid-September (foothills 9-16 %). No ground motion above +/-15 mm (2 sigma) in 120 days. Soil moisture did not separate irrigated floor from foothills. Tonle Sap: newly flooded pixels have coherence 0.12-0.22 but dry land also loses coherence, so coherence confirms and cannot map alone.
studies.verdict: coherence shipped as Ararat layers; motion and soil moisture not detected / not useful

studies.question: Can the Ararat coherence results be shown in the app?
studies.method: Export layers and a share-of-valley-floor series to the app data.
studies.result: Layers added to the Ararat place (commit 756746e); synthetic tests only for the exporter.
studies.verdict: shipped

studies.question: Did NISAR record the Tibet M7.0 earthquake (22 October)?
studies.method: L2 GUNW pair across the event and a control pair before it on the same track and frame; far-field ramp removed; peak to peak within a radius of the USGS epicentre.
studies.result: 127 cm peak to peak within 45 km (control 4.7 cm); about ten fringes; far-field sd 1.3 cm (0.7); processing variants 119-138 cm.
studies.verdict: shipped (event place); not checked against GNSS

studies.result: Ascending 50 cm, descending 55 cm within 60 km (controls 11.6 / 10.2 cm). The M7.5 40 s later is in the same pairs.

studies.result: Descending 133 cm, ascending 85 cm within 60 km (controls 21 / 15 cm); descending 107-165 cm across processing variants, least stable; 4 of 5 pixels near the epicentre lost.

studies.result: Venezuela M7.5: descending 48 cm (control 10.8), 1,062 km2 above 10 cm (control 8); ascending only 9 % valid pixels. Qaidam M5.6: one compact patch 3-4 km across in three independent pairs, about 10 km2 above 5 cm (controls 0).

studies.result: Not detected: Flores Sea M7.8, Mexico M7.3, Sanriku M6.9, Qinghai M5.8, Khuzdar M5.7, Redwood Valley M5.6, Turangi M5.7, Qaidam M5.3. Marginal: Huancayo M5.5. Reasons in the negative-results table.

studies.method: Coherence in event pair against a control pair, loss patch rule (control at least 0.45, event below 0.35, drop at least 0.25, patch at least 12 pixels at 80 m).
studies.result: 8.5 km2 patch at the site (next largest 1.8 km2); control coherence 0.65 to 0.14 at those pixels; descending 5.0 km2. A -11 to +4 cm motion lead is not claimed.

Patch areas are threshold dependent and not claimed.

studies.question: Can small networks reproduce the maths and add anything?
studies.method: Temporal autoencoder (19,546 parameters) and small U-Net; v1 on loose physics labels, v2 on math-detector labels with season channels.
studies.result: v1 copied its rules and over-called (Tonle Sap 10,149 km2 on 17 October against 3,837); v2 follows the physics rules within +/-4 %. No ground truth: agreement with another algorithm, not accuracy.
studies.verdict: U-Net v2 admitted as a fusion expert; adds a little (mountain false water 10.6 to 7.4 km2)

studies.question: Does a large ImageNet-pretrained network help?
studies.method: EfficientNet-B4 stages 0-3 as masked autoencoder, features clustered by a Gaussian mixture.
studies.result: Water agreement IoU 0.21 against 0.65 for a plain Gaussian mixture on the raw HH and HV; no better than its random twin; 316,805 parameters.
studies.verdict: rejected (documentation only)

studies.question: Can a transformer fill the 24-day outage pass?
studies.method: Masked-date transformer over ten dates with day-of-year time encoding; hide a real pass, predict it, compare with linear interpolation.
studies.result: About 2 % better than a straight line in time on pixel values in the strict test (15 % in the looser one); shoreline slightly worse (IoU 0.40 against 0.42).
studies.verdict: rejected for the map; estimate only if labelled

studies.question: Do open pretrained radar models help (Microsoft ai4g Sentinel-1 flood net; ALOS-2 L-band)?
studies.method: Load, smoke test, short fine-tune; ALOS-2 with Lake Sevan held out.
studies.result: ai4g without retraining IoU 0.390 against 0.389 for its own threshold rule; ALOS-2 balanced accuracy 0.91 at Sevan (random weights 0.67) against 0.99 for the math detector.
studies.verdict: rejected (documented only)

studies.question: Do learned speckle filters beat the current multi-temporal filter?
studies.method: Three small networks trained on the images themselves (noise-to-noise, blind spot, multi-temporal).
studies.result: Best learned filter balanced accuracy 0.9951 (Tonle Sap) and 0.9963 (Sevan) against 0.9957 and 0.9958; test noise +/-0.003; about three times more speckle-sized specks. Equivalent looks gained x1.1-1.5 against x2.5-3.1.
studies.verdict: rejected on previews (may pay off on calibrated 80 m and 20 m data)

studies.question: Can a physics autoencoder unmix pixels into water, flooded vegetation and land?
studies.method: Encoder plus a fixed radar-mixing decoder with a terrain prior.
studies.result: Sevan shoreline RMSE 0.507 against 0.354 for the analytic sub-pixel method; Tonle Sap open water 9,757 km2 on 17 October, far above the independent range. Best on synthetic scenes (RMSE 0.110 against 0.158 hard mask).
studies.verdict: rejected for the app (a talk item)

studies.question: Does a network trained on independent (Landsat) labels generalise to unseen places?
studies.method: U-Net trained on JRC-record labels at other places, tested on held-out places; compared with logistic regression.
studies.result: About equal to the math detector on unseen places (Sevan 0.994 against 0.989); below fusion v2 (0.9988; 6 against 99 km2 of false water on land); unseen Lake Chad 70 % of the lake against 99 % for fusion v2.
studies.verdict: evaluated only (cross-check)
